notes: TIER: robots.txt (curl) allows all ('Allow: /', only /account/, /checkout/, /wishlist/ disallowed) - proceeded with TIER 1 (direct HTTP via curl) for sitemap/robots, then TIER 2 (Playwright, local install found in the shared scratchpad node_modules) once it became clear this is a Next.js client-hydrated storefront where product grids/counts are populated by an internal REST API (www.foslighting.in/restapi/v1/product) rather than present in the raw SSR HTML - curl alone could see page titles/H1s and the site's sitemap.xml but not reliable product counts. DISCOVERY: fetched sitemap.xml (1515 URLs) and grepped for diwali/christmas/festive/holi/xmas/new-year/navratri/rakhi/raksha/eid/halloween/valentine/mother/father/thanksgiving - only two relevant nodes surfaced: /festive-lights (a general 'Festive Lights' product-type category: candle stands, tealight/votive holders, glass lanterns, string lights) and /festive-lights/diwali (a specific Diwali sub-page, title 'Diwali Festive Lights Online | Decorative Lights for Diwali 2024', banner 'BRIGHTEN UP YOUR HOME THIS FESTIVE SEASON WITH OUR DIWALI SPECIALS!'). VERIFICATION VIA PLAYWRIGHT: rendered /festive-lights/diwali and captured its network call to /restapi/v1/product?tags=Diwali+Special&categories=... which returned total:9 with items array length 9 (candle stands, tealight/votive holders, glass lanterns tagged 'Diwali Special', drawn from both the 'festive-lights' and 'sale' underlying categories - a curated cross-category Diwali collection, not a subset/duplicate of the plain Festive Lights category). Confirmed on-page: the main product grid at the top of the Diwali page (above the separate 'Featured Products' cross-sell section, which is a generic tags=Featured feed of 29 unrelated products used for gifting suggestions and correctly excluded) shows exactly 9 tiles with prices/QUICK VIEW, matching the API total exactly. EXCLUDED the parent 'Festive Lights' page (own PLP, displayed '5 products', https://www.foslighting.in/festive-lights) - its own on-page copy states it serves 'Diwali, Christmas, weddings, or family events' generically (candle stands/lanterns/string lights usable for any celebration), so it fails the rule-2 test of being associated with ONE specific holiday; this mirrors the explicit boundary rule that a category merely containing some seasonal products isn't itself a seasonal category. ABSENCE CHECKS (thorough, per Diwali-focus instruction and Mother's/Father's Day reminder): probed direct URL guesses for other festival sub-pages under both /festive-lights/<slug> and root /<slug> for christmas, new-year, navratri, holi, rakhi, raksha-bandhan, eid, valentine, valentines-day, mothers-day, fathers-day, thanksgiving, halloween, diwali-lights, diwali-decor, diyas, diwali, gifts, gift-guide, diwali-gifts, diwali-lighting - every one of these returned HTTP 200 but with the site's generic catch-all title 'Lighting Manufacturer In India | Buy Fancy Lighting Online India' (confirmed soft-404/no dedicated page), proving they are not real taxonomy nodes (a raw 200 status alone is not proof of existence on this Next.js app - title-scanned each to confirm). Also checked the homepage mega-nav (only 'FESTIVE LIGHTS' appears; hovering revealed no flyout submenu with additional festival items) and the full sitemap.xml keyword sweep. No Christmas, New Year, Navratri, Holi, Raksha Bandhan/Rakhi, Eid, Valentine's Day, Mother's Day, Father's Day, Thanksgiving, or Halloween category/PLP exists anywhere on the site - genuinely absent, not overlooked. 'Sale'/clearance page (/sale) is a storewide sale page unrelated to any specific holiday and was not considered. Only one genuine seasonal row found: Diwali.

rows.evidence: Dedicated Diwali PLP (title 'Diwali Festive Lights Online | Decorative Lights for Diwali 2024', on-page banner 'BRIGHTEN UP YOUR HOME THIS FESTIVE SEASON WITH OUR DIWALI SPECIALS!'). Main product grid shows exactly 9 product tiles (candle stands, tealight/votive holders, glass lanterns), matching the site's own internal REST API response (restapi/v1/product?tags=Diwali+Special&categories=...) which returned total:9, items.length:9, all tagged 'Diwali Special'.
